newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks lower on Dow, gold, copper falls.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks lower on Dow, gold, copper falls.

text.p: Australian shares opened weaker on Thursday after a 120 point drop on Wall Street and further falls in the gold and copper prices, but trade was quiet ahead of June employment data due out later this morning.
In opening trade, the All Ordinaries index was 23.2 points down at 2,672.9 with turnover worth about A$68.76 million (US$51 million).
Brokers said the market is likely to settle between 10 and 20 points lower, with the June jobs data unlikely to have much impact, unless the figures are outside the forecast range.
Unemployment rose to 8.8 percent in May and economists are expecting the jobless rate to be 8.7 percent in June and for employment to rise.
"Wall Street is off 120 so I think there will be a few fireworks around," said one Melbourne-based broker. The Dow industrials failed to hit the 8,000 mark and ended at 7,842.
The gold price lost all of its gains from Tuesday's bounce, while the copper price neared four-and-a-half year lows.

"I don't think anybody really expected the gold price to do any serious bouncing and as far as the copper price is concerned, I think people have pulled back the expectations on the copper outlook," the broker said.
Gold miners Newcrest and Normandy topped the turnover lists on Thursday, with Newcrest losing ground but Normandy remaining unchanged.
Resource sectors fell harder than the industrials. Rio Tinto, BHP and WMC all of which have copper operations, were the biggest fallers amongst the miners.
